editorial:
You are dropped onto a cold, rocky island where two men run a lighthouse in the 1890s. One is an old, grumpy keeper who guards the light like treasure. The other is a younger worker trying to earn his pay and keep his head down. At first, their days are filled with chores, bad food, and awkward talks. Then the weather turns, the supply ship does not come, and the island starts to feel like a trap. The movie is black and white, square-shaped, and full of strange sounds, so it feels like an old nightmare you cannot wake from.

The acting is the big draw. Both leads give raw, loud, physical performances, and you can feel their anger and fear. The pacing is slow at first, then gets wild, so you need patience. It is funny in a dark way, but also gross and intense. If you want a normal plot, this may frustrate you. If you like weird, tense stories, it is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the younger keeper finally reaches the top of the lighthouse and looks into the light. The movie never shows what he sees, but his reaction suggests something huge and terrible. He falls down the stairs and is attacked by seagulls, then left broken on the rocks. The older keeper may have been a ghost, a memory, or a trick of the island. The ending leaves you unsure if any of it was real, but it makes clear that chasing the light destroyed him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange, intense character stories.
